source_book: Sri Chaitanya — FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students, Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition)
note: Question index for diffing and authoring. Stems restated in our own wording; the mathematics is exact. No solution content from the source book appears in this file, by policy.

chapter.printed_title: INTRODUCTION TO THREE DIMENSIONAL COORDINATE GEOMETRY

questions.stem: Find the centroid of the triangle whose vertices are (5, 4, 6), (1, −1, 3) and (4, 3, 2).
questions.notes: Printed with no imperative verb — 'The centroid of the triangle whose vertices are …' — the instruction 'Find' is supplied here. Star prefix sits in the clipped spine gutter; three glyphs readable, the first only partly.

questions.stem: If (3, 2, −1), (4, 1, 1) and (6, 2, 5) are three vertices and (4, 2, 2) is the centroid of a tetrahedron, find the fourth vertex.
questions.notes: Star prefix sits in the clipped spine gutter; three glyphs readable, the first only partly.

questions.stem: Find the coordinates of the vertex C of triangle ABC if its centroid is the origin and the vertices A, B are (1, 1, 1) and (−2, 4, 1) respectively.
Find the centroid of the tetrahedron whose vertices are (2, 3, −4), (−3, 3, 2), (−1, 4, 2) and (3, 5, 1).
Find x if the distance between (5, −1, 7) and (x, 5, 1) is 9 units.
Find the fourth vertex of the parallelogram whose consecutive vertices are (2, 4, −1), (3, 6, −1) and (4, 5, 1).
Find the ratio in which the XZ plane divides the line joining A(−2, 3, 4) and B(1, 2, 3).
questions.notes: Unlike question 8, this one asks only for the ratio — it does not ask for the point of intersection.

questions.stem: Find the ratio in which the YZ plane divides the line joining A(2, 4, 5) and B(3, 5, −4). Also find the point of intersection.
Show that the points (1, 2, 3), (7, 0, 1) and (−2, 3, 4) are collinear.
Show that the points (1, 2, 3), (2, 3, 1) and (3, 1, 2) form an equilateral triangle.
questions.notes: Printed 'from an equilateral triangle' — 'form' is meant. The number carries no star prefix and is fully legible.

questions.stem: If the point (1, 2, 3) is changed to the point (2, 3, 1) through translation of axes, find the new origin.
questions.notes: The question number sits in the clipped spine gutter; no star prefix is visible, so 0 is recorded as the readable value and may be understated. Note this is a translation-of-axes question printed inside the 3D-coordinates chapter.
